questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why Taylor Swift is so popular
How earthquakes damage concert stadiums
Whether dancing fans at a Taylor Swift concert caused an earthquake
How seismologists predict earthquakes
questions.why: They hear about the 'Swift-quake' and whether it really was an earthquake.

questions.q: What does Phil mean when he says Taylor Swift 'literally rocks the world'?
options: Her fans' dancing actually made the ground move
Her music makes people's lives more enjoyable and exciting
She sings rock music
She has performed in every country
questions.why: He says her fans' dancing 'literally moved the Earth', with seismic activity detected miles away.

questions.q: What was detected after the Edinburgh concert?
options: Damage to buildings near the stadium
A crack in the ground
Loud noise heard across the city
Seismic activity four miles away
questions.why: Phil says seismic activity was detected four miles away.

questions.q: What did seismologists Emma Greenough and James Panton want to find out?
options: Whether Taylor Swift's music was too loud for people living nearby
Whether the same effect would happen at her Cardiff concert
How many fans went to the Edinburgh show
Whether earthquakes can stop concerts
questions.why: They wanted to see if the same thing would happen at Taylor's concert in Cardiff.

questions.q: According to James Panton, what caused the peak on his graph?
options: The very loud sound coming from the speakers on the stage
A small natural earthquake
Traffic outside the stadium
73,000 fans jumping and stamping at the same time
questions.why: He says it's the energy from the 73,000 people 'jumping in unison and stamping in unison'.

questions.q: What does the measurement of 23 nanometres show?
options: How far the fans jumped
How much the ground bent up and down
How deep a crack in the ground under the stadium was
How far away the sound travelled
questions.why: James says it means the ground was flexing up and down by 23 nanometres.

questions.q: Was the concert's effect as strong as an earthquake?
options: No, when compared it is generally less than magnitude one
Yes, it was a small earthquake
Yes, it was actually stronger than most of the earthquakes in the UK
Nobody has tried to compare them
questions.why: James says 'definitely not', and converted magnitudes are generally less than one.

questions.q: Why wasn't the concert officially an earthquake?
options: Because it lasted less than a minute
Because it happened at night
Because a real earthquake must break the earth's crust
Because it wasn't recorded by the scientists' equipment in Edinburgh
questions.why: Georgie says by definition an earthquake must break the earth's crust, caused by plates or a volcano.
